description: Runtime kill switches wired into the live execution path + periodic reconciliation job (PRIORITY 4). Today kill switches exist only as in-memory registries (packages/observability/src/kill-switch.ts, packages/payment-sdk/src/kill-switch.ts) and are NOT consulted by the worker's real-lifecycle path, and there is no periodic job that resolves INDETERMINATE/orphaned transactions. Add a durable kill-switch store in Postgres, evaluate active kill switches (scopes: platform/merchant/wallet/agent/mandate/connector/payment_adapter) as a gate BEFORE any consequential external effect in the worker path, and add a periodic reconciliation job that runs in the worker to scan for INDETERMINATE/orphaned transactions and resolve them against authoritative provider/merchant evidence.
steps: Add migration packages/data/migrations/0008-kill-switches.up.sql (+ .down.sql) creating runtime.kill_switches (id identity PK, environment, scope text CHECK scope IN ('platform','merchant','wallet','agent','mandate','connector','payment_adapter'), entity_id text NULL, status text CHECK status IN ('active','inactive') DEFAULT 'active', reason text NOT NULL, activated_by text NOT NULL, activated_at timestamptz DEFAULT clock_timestamp(), expires_at timestamptz NULL, UNIQUE(environment, scope, entity_id)). Match 0005 DDL style. Bump migration version expectations in the migration tests accordingly (this stacks on 0007 from FEAT-001).

Add a PostgresKillSwitchStore in packages/data (recordActivate, deactivate, listActive(environment), isActive(scope, entityId, now)) reusing the KillSwitchScope vocabulary from @counter/observability if importable without a depcruise violation; otherwise define the scope union locally in data and keep it in sync. Export from packages/data/src/index.ts. Treat status='active' AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now) as active.

Add a LifecyclePolicyPort-compatible kill-switch gate to the worker path. In apps/worker/src/real-lifecycle.ts the policy.allow(request) gate already runs BEFORE any external effect; add a KillSwitchGatePort (injected via RealLifecycleConfig) that is consulted in that same pre-effect position: if a platform kill switch OR a merchant kill switch for config.merchantId (OR connector/payment_adapter) is active, DENY -> return a declined outcome with providerReference 'kill-switch-blocked:<key>' and create NO external effect. Wire the real PostgresKillSwitchStore in boot.ts/main.ts.

Add a creds+DB gated integration test proving the kill switch blocks a real checkout: activate a merchant kill switch for the pilot merchant in runtime.kill_switches, run the real lifecycle, assert the outcome is declined/blocked and that NO Shopify order and NO Razorpay order were created (query the store/provider to confirm zero effect). Clean up: deactivate/delete the kill-switch row. Skip cleanly without creds/DB.

Add a periodic reconciliation job to the worker. Implement a reconciliation scanner (e.g. apps/worker/src/reconciliation-job.ts) that, on an interval, scans for transactions left in INDETERMINATE/orphaned state (using the durable step ledger from FEAT-001 and/or outbox receipt rows with phase INDETERMINATE) and resolves each against authoritative evidence: query the real Shopify order (connector.orderQuery) and/or Razorpay to determine the true terminal state, then record the resolution durably (advance to CLOSED-equivalent or leave INDETERMINATE with updated evidence). Preserve explicit outcomes; never fabricate a success. Register it in main.ts alongside the worker loop with graceful shutdown, guarded by an env flag so it is inert in unit tests.

Add unit tests for the reconciliation scanner (deterministic, in-memory ledger + mock connector) covering: an INDETERMINATE txn whose provider evidence shows a completed order -> resolved to closed; an INDETERMINATE txn with no provider effect -> stays/records indeterminate with evidence; an already-CLOSED txn -> no-op. Add a gated integration variant if feasible that seeds an INDETERMINATE ledger row against the real DB and asserts the scanner resolves it, cleaning up afterward.
acceptance_criteria: Migrations 0008 apply/rollback cleanly; migration version expectations updated and passing.
packages/data exposes a PostgresKillSwitchStore with an isActive check honoring status + expires_at.
The worker real-lifecycle path consults kill switches BEFORE any external effect; an active platform/merchant/connector/payment_adapter kill switch yields a blocked outcome with ZERO external effect.
Gated integration test: enabling a merchant kill switch blocks a real checkout with no Shopify/Razorpay effect and cleans up.

A periodic reconciliation job runs in the worker (env-guarded), scans for INDETERMINATE/orphaned transactions, and resolves them against authoritative provider evidence; covered by unit tests and (if feasible) a gated integration test.
Existing 2764 tests still pass; depcruise clean.
verification: source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && find apps/worker -name '*.tsbuildinfo' -delete; rm -rf apps/worker/dist; pnpm build
pnpm test (baseline green; new unit tests pass; gated integration tests skip without creds)
With creds+DB exported: run the kill-switch-blocks-checkout integration test and the reconciliation integration test; confirm pass and clean store/DB
findings:
Implemented in 4 commits (a9a0785 data, f3510b3 kill-switch worker, a268f77 reconciliation, b1e9282 reconcile integration test). Kill switches: migration 0008-kill-switches (runtime.kill_switches; partial unique indexes for platform-null vs scoped entity_id; CHECK enforces scoped-requires-entity; active = status='active' AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at>now)); PostgresKillSwitchStore in packages/data/src/runtime-repositories.ts (recordActivate/deactivate/listActive/isActive, Result returns, env 'local'); exported from index.ts. Scope union defined LOCALLY in @counter/data (KILL_SWITCH_SCOPES) to avoid a new depcruise edge to @counter/observability; kept in sync with observability + the 0008 CHECK. Worker gate: added KillSwitchGatePort to real-lifecycle.ts consulted BEFORE the policy allow gate and before ANY external effect; an active platform/merchant/connector/payment_adapter switch returns declined with providerReference 'kill-switch-blocked:<key>' and ZERO effect. Wired PostgresKillSwitchStore-backed gate via createPostgresKillSwitchGatePort in boot.ts (checks platform, merchant:<pilotMerchantId>, connector:shopify, payment_adapter:razorpay) and threaded through selectPaymentAuthorizationPort's new DurableStores param in main.ts (alongside the durable step ledger). Reconciliation: reconciliation-job.ts (reconcileCandidate/runReconciliationPass/startReconciliationJob/reconciliationEnabled) resolves INDETERMINATE txns against authoritative Shopify order state via connector.orderQuery — settled(PAID/PARTIALLY_REFUNDED/REFUNDED)->resolved_closed; no durable order reference->no_provider_effect; unsettled or inconclusive query->still_indeterminate; already-resolved->no-op; NEVER fabricates success. reconciliation-boot.ts wires the Postgres-backed source (INDETERMINATE outbox receipts without a resolved_closed follow-up), ledger reader (runtime.lifecycle_steps finalize reference), order query, and recorder (appends transaction.reconciliation.v1 outbox events). Registered in main.ts guarded by RECONCILIATION_ENABLED + real connector mode with graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT shutdown (stop() awaits in-flight pass before closing DB). Migration version assertions bumped 7->8 in migrations.integration.test.ts and rls.integration.test.ts. VERIFICATION: pnpm build + pnpm depcruise (0 violations, 2089 modules) + pnpm test all green — 2776 passed (baseline 2766 + 10 new unit tests: 7 reconciliation + 3 kill-switch gate), 6 skipped (gated integration tests skip cleanly without creds). Ran BOTH gated integration tests against REAL DB + Shopify + Razorpay: kill-switch-blocks-checkout PASSED (declined kill-switch-blocked:*, ZERO ledger rows) and reconciliation-job.integration PASSED (real PAID order -> resolved_closed). Cleaned up: verified 0 residual kill_switches/lifecycle_steps/outbox rows after runs. Migration 0008 up/down round-trip verified in a rolled-back txn against live DB (partial unique + CHECK enforced) without touching live schema. NOTES: real-lifecycle mark-paid can transiently return 'Order is temporarily unavailable to be modified' right after finalize; the reconciliation integration test retries mark-paid (as the real lifecycle does) before asserting PAID. Sandbox file-edit overlay diverges from real disk — all edits were made via bash heredoc and verified with git/bash.

--- REVIEW FOLLOWUP (2026-08-27 review: NEEDS_CHANGES) ---
Issue 1 (BLOCKING — reconciliation key mismatch): the receipt sink wrote the DERIVED transaction CounterId (deriveTransactionId(payload.transactionId)) as the receipt's transactionId, while the step ledger is keyed on the RAW payload.transactionId, so the candidate->ledger join never matched in the deployed wiring and every candidate degraded to no_provider_effect. FIX: TransactionReceipt now carries an explicit idempotencyKey (the raw reference), set in the handler from payload.transactionId; main.ts's outbox receipt sink writes it into the receipt payload's `idempotencyKey` field; reconciliation-boot.ts's candidate source reads THAT (COALESCE fallback to transactionId for legacy rows) and looks up the ledger with it; the recorder + isResolved + candidate SELECT all key on idempotencyKey. Proven live end-to-end: the reconciliation integration test now drives the REAL lifecycle handler (so deriveTransactionId actually runs), asserts the receipt's stamped transactionId is a derived ctr_transaction_ id DISTINCT from the raw key, and confirms the scanner joins on the raw key and resolves the real settled Shopify order to resolved_closed (passed against real Shopify + live DB).
Issue 4 (unbounded re-recording): isResolved treated only resolved_closed as resolved and the candidate SELECT only excluded resolved_closed, so a permanently-orphaned no_provider_effect appended a new reconciliation outbox row every pass forever. FIX: no_provider_effect is now treated as a TERMINAL resolved disposition (still_indeterminate stays re-scannable so a later settlement can close it); both isResolved and the candidate SELECT exclude ('resolved_closed','no_provider_effect'). Added deterministic unit tests proving the scan is idempotent for an orphaned candidate and still re-scans a not-yet-settled one.
